points.description: States that infinite recursion can be caused by the recursive step being defined incorrectly (e.g. the recursive call does not move towards the base case, or the step is wrong). Equivalent wording such as 'the recursive case is faulty' earns the mark.
States that infinite recursion can be caused by the base case being missing (not included in the definition). Equivalent wording such as 'no stopping condition' earns the mark.
